newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MOL soars to record after wage settlement.
newsitem.headline: MOL soars to record after wage settlement.

text.p: Share prices in Hungarian oil and gas company MOL Rt exceeded the 3,000 forint psychological barrier in early trading on the Budapest Stock Exchange following news of a 17 percent wage settlement for 1997.
MOL shares opened at 2,800 forints, below Thursday's close of 2,850 forints, and by 1149 GMT it soared seven percent to a record level of 3,060 forints.
The company said this morning it had agreed with trade unions to raise basic wages by an average 17 percent in 1997.
"Fears of a possible strike were dispelled by this news," one trader said.
MOL and the trade unions also agreed to provide employees with a one-off share package worth half the average basic wage.
Newspaper reports said in early January that Hungary's Oil Industry Trade Union was claiming an immediate 30 percent wage increase, as against 15 percent offered by the company from next July.
They quoted union sources as saying talks with employers were inconclusive and further deadlock could lead to strike action.
But MOL's statement on Friday also denied earlier press reports, saying there was no threat of strike or actual strike at either of its divisions.
